Two numbers (1 working and 1 standby) of multistage, electric motor-driven boiler feed pumps (BFP) are considered to serve the feed water requirement of the boilers. Each BFP is installed along with a variable speed fluid coupling. The total capacity of the pumps is suitable for a 120% maximum continuous rating of the boiler output, including the spray water requirement of the attemperator. 5.3 Process Flow Diagram of Steam and Condensate Network The process flow diagram (PFD) and heat and materials balance (H&MB) of the steam and condensate network are given in Figure 4. Attachment-7: Initial Engineering Design and Cost Estimate 17 DE-FE0031937 / 0009 5.4 Process Description A single gas turbine (GT) unit generates 58 MW of power. The MP steam (615 PSIA, 750oF) is generated from the HRSG unit by utilizing the sensible heat of GT exhaust gas and supplementary firing of NG (Duct firing). MP steam produced from the HRSG is sent to the Back pressure steam turbine (BPT) through the BPT inlet steam header. The BPT generates 15 MW of power utilizing the energy of MP steam and generates low-pressure (LP) steam. The LP steam from BPT and steam boilers is sent to the LP steam header and is tapped nearby the process units. Additionally, LP process steam is also generated from the WGS boiler. All the condensate generated from CCS and WGS island is headed to a condensate mixing drum. A common deaerator with feed water storage is considered for preheating and deaerating the condensate return water from the process units and DM make-up water. 5.5 Process and Instrument Diagram of CHP and Boiler The process & instrument diagram (P&ID) of CHP unit, BPT and boilers are given in Annexure 2, and the list is shown in Table 16.
